answer.rationale: Rollback is blocked by compliance. Regional failover during settlement peak risks duplicating in-flight writes. Adding capacity doesn't address the latency regression introduced by the new release. A circuit breaker would shed load but risk losing writes at peak settlement. Memory b5 (day 55) is the closest analog: routing report/read-heavy queries off the primary relieved write-path pressure and the primary recovered same-day. Today's settlement peak is write-heavy, so the primary is saturated; offloading all read traffic (dashboard queries, status checks, reconciliation reads) to replicas is the lowest-risk single intervention that directly reduces write-path contention without touching the release, without shedding writes, and without moving data across regions. The security patch stays in place, writes stay on the primary, and latency relief comes from removing competing read load. Because I can verify only one memory, I pick b5 to confirm the read-replica routing details and any caveats before committing.
